summary: The last 4 weeks show a fragmented, low-volume training block with only 9 sessions logged — notably absent are pool swims and structured run sessions, which is concerning given the Marathon is just 120 days away. Sleep is chronically insufficient, with many nights under 4 hours and body battery readings frequently in the low single digits, indicating significant accumulated fatigue that will blunt adaptation. The nearest priority must be the Marathon: running volume and consistency are dangerously low relative to a sub-4h goal, and the upcoming weeks need to build steady aerobic run base immediately.
suggestions: Sleep is your biggest limiter right now — multiple nights of under 3.5 hours and body battery readings of 0–7 are unsustainable; prioritise 7–8 hours consistently this week before adding any training load.

Running consistency is critically low (only one run logged in 4 weeks at a high HR of 169 bpm for 10 km) — with the Marathon 120 days away, begin building an easy aerobic run base immediately at 6:30–7:00/km, targeting at least 3 runs per week.

The 5K Open Water Swim on Oct 25 is well-served by your recent swim sessions (5.2 km open water on Oct 3), but avoid high-intensity cycling the day before — keep Oct 24 ride at the lower end of Z2 and shorten if fatigue is high.

On Oct 15, the planned 6×800 m intervals are premature given you've had only one run in 4 weeks at already-high HR — replace with a continuous easy aerobic run to rebuild run fitness safely before reintroducing intensity.
Pool swimming has been completely absent despite two open water sessions — add at least two pool swims per week going forward to improve technique and pacing control ahead of the OWS race on Oct 25.
